title: DiscPuter
summary: USB CD-ROM emulator: carry OS installer ISOs, boot a computer from them
description:
DiscPuter turns the CardputerZero into a USB optical drive. Keep installer images on the SD card, plug the CardputerZero into a computer and it sees a CD-ROM with the disc you picked on the CardputerZero's own screen.

- CD-ROM mode for ISO 9660 / UDF images (installers, live CDs), read-only USB disk mode for .img files and hybrid Linux ISOs; AUTO picks one from what is in the image
- Images are recognised: volume label, bootable (El Torito), hybrid, MBR / GPT
- Insert, eject and swap discs; the computer is reconnected so it notices the new disc
- Copy images in over USB: the CardputerZero becomes a flash drive DISCPUTER; copy .iso files onto it, eject it, and they move into the image list by themselves
- Keys 4-8 under the screen: eject, reconnect, mode, stop, insert

How to connect: Host/Slave switch on Slave, cable on the RIGHT USB-C (in Slave the USB hub, Ethernet and USB-A are off).

Root: the USB gadget needs it. The package installs a small helper (/usr/lib/cz-discputer/dp-gadget) that only accepts images in ~/discputer/images, /media or /mnt. On the first run the app asks for your user's password once and adds a sudo rule for that helper only (/etc/sudoers.d/cz-discputer, checked with visudo); removing the package removes the rule.

Not yet: BIN/CUE and CD audio (planned). Inspired by USBODE (danifunker), GPL-3.0.
